use_case_summary: Silverpine runs a B2B SaaS analytics product that uses LLMs for automated ticket summarization, contextual doc-search, and personalized in-app assistants. They need parity with current provider for output (especially action-item extraction), predictable latency for interactive assistants (<400ms p95), and a path from Hosted (fast onboarding) to Dedicated (VPC + capacity guarantees) within one quarter.
notes:
Background: currently using another LLM API provider (primarily for chat + summarization). Looking to migrate due to rising cost and desire for predictable latency and a private tenancy option. Customer is mid-market with compliance needs (SOC2) and some EU data residency requirements.

POC summary (hosted):
- Scope: ticket summarization (priority), doc-search, and re-ranking for search results. 10k sample tickets + 120k docs.
- Runs: 3 prompt variants for summarization; batch eval set of 2k queries.
- Metrics captured: ROUGE/F1 for extraction (action items), human-blind preference tests (n=30 agents), latency p50/p95/p99, cost per 1M tokens.
- Findings: Redwood Hosted achieved similar human preference for generic summaries but we saw regressions in action-item extraction on ~14% of cases vs incumbent. Latency p95 improved from 820ms (incumbent) -> 360ms (Redwood hosted) under same concurrency. Estimated hosted cost 1M tokens: ~ $210 (vs incumbent $260) given caching/kv savings.

Technical notes on regressions and compat layer:
- Root cause analysis: subtle prompt-role differences (incumbent injected extra role tokens), tokenizer boundary handling (truncated trailing punctuation differently), and default stop-sequence behavior.
- Compat approaches evaluated: 1) lightweight API compatibility shim that rewrites prompts/stops to mimic incumbent behavior; 2) small prompt template adjustments and few-shot exemplars; 3) model variant selection and temperature tuning for tighter extraction.
- SE action items: run token-diff tool (Priya) across 200 failing samples; add explicit end-of-summary token in templates; test explicit "Action Items:" anchor; evaluate KV cache warm-up for repeated ticket threads.

Customer quotes / sentiment: "We like the latency and cost story but cannot accept regression on summary action-items — this is core to our support SLAs." — Head of Product.

Commercials & timeline:
- Wants Hosted POC -> Dedicated migration in same quarter if regressions are resolved. Q2 procurement window (forecast 2026-05).
- Interested in 3 sizing options: small (reserved for dev + canary), medium (production baseline), large (peak season throughput). Prefers annual commit if unit economics are compelling.

Next steps (short):
- SE deliver tokenization diff report (by 2026-03-10).
- Run dedicated-config bench (cost/latency projection) and share final pricing by 2026-03-14.
- Legal: negotiate DPA/data-residency clause (customer provided EU-specific reqs).
- Schedule migration POC (hosted->dedicated) to validate parity once fixes applied.
